title: introduce-presubmit-prober-and-prune-legacy-makefiles
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add lightweight presubmit prober for fast PR feedback; remove legacy top-level Makefiles and plumbing; unify toolchain images to rw-tiny-builder; bump several GH Actions and regen lockfiles. No runtime behavior changes to prod services.
commits_summary: 5 commits: (1) add presubmit prober binary and workflow; (2) introduce rw-tiny-builder Dockerfile + publish job; (3) remove legacy Makefile targets and update CONTRIBUTING.md; (4) bump actions/checkout@v4->v5 and actions/setup-go@v4; (5) regen lockfiles and fix linter warnings.
description:
Context and motivation: Our presubmit lane has grown slow and brittle; a full test/LT run costs expensive runner time and masks fast-to-catch repo hygiene regressions. This PR introduces a small presubmit prober (Go binary) that runs a curated fast-check suite (lint surface, license header, simple import hygiene, minimal static checks) in ~20s on rw-tiny-builder image. It also prunes legacy top-level Makefiles and related plumbing that caused duplicate build semantics across services.

What this PR does (single string): Adds a dedicated GitHub workflow (.github/workflows/presubmit-prober.yml) that runs on PR open/sync; introduces images/rw-tiny-builder used to run fast checks deterministically; adds tools/presubmit/prober written in Go (intended to be compiled into a ~3.5MB static binary) which performs: - staged-go-mod-checks, - minimal eslint quickpass, - header/license enforcement, - fast import reorder detection. Removes old Makefile targets in /Makefile and build/Makefile.old and updates CONTRIBUTING.md to point to the new lightweight presubmit path. Bumps key GH Actions to their current stable (actions/checkout to v5, setup-go to v4) and regenerates lockfiles for package.json and go.sum. Adds a small publish step for rw-tiny-builder (internal-only) and a short note in docs about when to run the full CI.

Checklist: - [x] Add presubmit prober code and tests for core checks - [x] Add workflow and RBAC-safe publish job - [x] Update docs and CONTRIBUTING - [x] Bump GH Actions and regen locks - [x] Remove legacy Makefile entries - [x] Validate on a set of active repos (see test plan)

Test plan: Ran the new workflow in a forked repo across 12 active microservices; prober correctly flagged missing license headers and bad imports, completed in 18–25s on GitHub-hosted runners. End-to-end CI (full test suite) was executed once to ensure the Makefile removals didn't break release pipelines. Manual run of release automation against a staging repo validated that release signing and artifact paths remain unchanged.

Rollout & migration: The presubmit-prober workflow is opt-in by default for legacy repositories; we propose enabling it org-wide after a 2-week pilot. Removing Makefile targets is safe because all internal CI relies on curated scripts under ci/scripts/ and the new rw-tiny-builder reproduces the small steps that the removed Makefiles provided. If a repo needs the old targets, a migration note in CONTRIBUTING points to a one-line shim.

Follow-ups: (1) add granular metric reporting from prober to the Console for quick-fail histograms (ENG-4199). (2) Expand quick-checks to include a shallow unit-test smoke harness for languages that support it.

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the presubmit prober focused and avoids adding long-running tests to the quick lane; long tests remain in the nightly/integration lanes.
review_conversation:
Liam: "Looks good overall but can we avoid introducing another published image? Please ensure image size < 50MB compressed."
Maya: "rw-tiny-builder is intentionally tiny; Dockerfile uses distroless and multi-stage build. I added a size-check in publish action and examples showing how to run the binary locally."
Rhea: "Why remove the top-level Makefile? Some repos still use it in CI glue."
Maya: "Top-level Makefile had duplicated targets; CI glue uses ci/scripts/* now. I left a one-line shim text in CONTRIBUTING for edge cases and documented how to enable a compatibility target."
Ethan: "CI flaked on windows runners initially."
Maya: "Fixed by guarding OS-specific checks and adding explicit timeouts; reran CI and green."
Approvals: Liam approved after size check added on 2025-11-19; Rhea approved 2025-11-20. Merge performed by Maya after rebase and squash.
ci_summary: Checks run: presubmit-prober (only) -> pass; unit & integration matrix -> initially 2/24 jobs failed (flake in windows runner), rerun fixed; lint -> pass after minor fixes; release smoke -> pass. Notable: image-size-check added and passed. Final status: all checks green and protected-branch requirements satisfied.
merge_outcome: Merged to main on 2025-11-20 via squash by Maya Patel. Commit message squashed into: chore: presubmit prober + rw-tiny-builder; remove legacy Makefiles; bump actions; regen lockfiles.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental removal of Makefile targets used by bespoke repos. Mitigation: one-line migration shims in CONTRIBUTING, staged rollout opt-in for 2 weeks, and fast rollback by restoring Makefile.old if required. Presubmit prober is non-blocking until org-wide enablement.
test_plan_summary: Pilot across 12 repos, manual release smoke in staging, CI reruns for flaky windows jobs. Recorded timing metrics and false-positive rate < 1% during pilot.
notes_for_maintainers: To add new quick checks, extend tools/presubmit/checks.go and run `make prober-build` using rw-tiny-builder image. Publishing the builder requires team infra token; see .github/actions/publish-builder/README.md.
